problem: Find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola $x=5\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of a Hyperbola Given its Parametric Equations
examples.problem: Find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola with the parametric equations $x = 6\sec{t},\, y = 4 \sqrt{2}\tan{t}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola, we need to eliminate the parameter $t.$ We can do this using the secant-tangent identity.

- Isolating the $\sec t$ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =6\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \frac{x}{6} & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ {(\frac{x}{6})}^{2} & ={(\operatorname{sec}⁡t)}^{2} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{6}^{2}} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{36} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

- Isolating the $\tan{t}$ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{y}{4\sqrt{2}} & =\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ {(\frac{y}{4\sqrt{2}})}^{2} & ={(\operatorname{tan}⁡t)}^{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{{(4\sqrt{2})}^{2}} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{32} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the two equations into the identity $\tan^2{t} + 1 = \sec^2{t}$ and rearranging, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡t+1 & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{32}+1 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{36} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{36}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{32} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(\pm a,0).$ From the graph, we have that $(\sqrt{6},0)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=\sqrt{6}.$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}x,$ and so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{a} & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{b}{\sqrt{6}} & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ b & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
